correctness.rationale: The Pythagorean identity gives the exact conditional progress eigenvalue; boundary weights give zero while interior weights give positive progress. For the reciprocal objective F=λ_max(Σ_i v_i v_iᵀ/p_i) with v_i the columns of U⁻¹, the top-eigenspace subgradient at an interior minimizer is represented by a PSD trace-one Z. The Lagrange multiplier is F(p*) after summing the stationarity equations against p_i*, so v_iᵀZv_i=F(p*)p_i*²>0. Testing with this Z and using strict Cauchy–Schwarz in Σ_i(v_iᵀZv_i)/p_i proves unrestricted uniqueness, hence exchangeability. For ordinary weights (1−p)/m the transverse mode is t(1−p), t=(1−c)/m, and the core block has diagonal p,a(1−p) and off-diagonal r√(p(1−p)). The discriminant quadratic Q=Ap²+Bp+C satisfies 4AC−B²=16r²(a−r²)>0, giving strict concavity of the lower core root. Substitution at p_s=(a+r)/(1+a+2r) gives λ_s=(a−r²)/(1+a+2r) as the lower root (the two shifted diagonal entries are positive), with zero derivative. There the core minus transverse gap is Θ/[m(1+a+2r)]. If positive, the increasing core crosses the decreasing transverse line first; the determinant at t(1−p) is (1−p)[(c−r²)p−ct(1−p)], yielding the displayed crossing and its value. At Θ=0 both branches coincide. Uniformity follows because p_s>1/(m+1), while p_c equals that value iff r=c, which is in the crossing branch. In the singular family the core branch applies; mΛ_unif tends to the smaller root (2+α−√(α²+4β²))/2, below the transverse limit 1. Rationalizing yields the stated ratio and its divergence across families with β²=α+1/2.
residual_risks: Sharp one-step conditional coefficient only; not an annealed random-product exponent, adaptive selection result, or timing comparison. The stated Gram range is understood within positive c,r.

evidence: In the inverse of the row Gram, exceptional-to-ordinary entries are negative; the ordinary off-diagonal entries have sign sign(r²−c), by the Schur complement (1−c)I+(c−r²)11ᵀ. Flipping the exceptional row makes the entire inverse nonnegative exactly for r²≥c. Any sign switch making all exceptional entries nonnegative must give the ordinary rows a common sign, so cannot fix negative ordinary off-diagonals when r²<c.

For r²≥c, the all-ones inverse formula in the switched Gram gives p_s and λ_s. The singular scaling lies in that slice and follows from it plus the elementary uniform Gram eigenvalue. The positive-Θ crossing necessarily has r²<c.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The frozen comparison with inverse positivity needs the sign-switch qualification. Older exact coverage is partial, not an evaluation of the full threshold or of the branch in which the optimizing eigenvalue has both core and transverse directions.

The SDP and the inverse-positive slice (including the singular example after row sign switching) are covered and are not separately credited. A later documented catalogue publication gives an exact matching classification; this overlap is acknowledged without a claim about authorship or historical dependence.

value.rationale: The complete branch boundary is a meaningful exact benchmark for choosing fixed sampling among correlated equations with one outlier. It tells when a simple core design stops controlling worst-direction progress and when the transverse cluster mode determines the optimum, with global rather than assumed-symmetric uniqueness. This value does not depend on claiming the sign-switch-covered asymptotic example as new.
residual_risks: No claimed relationship to multi-step-optimal weights or wall-clock savings.
